rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fabricating reports includes inventing or altering a text or chain, misattributing reliable or weak reports, and falsely presenting a nonexistent saying as agreed upon.
rows.anchor: Rivayetlerde söylediği şekilde mevcud bile olmayan bir sözü müttefekun aleyh göstermesi ise böyle bir vaz‘olmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Finding evidence, comparing reports, distinguishing reliable from weak material, reconciling conflicts, and deriving results are praiseworthy scholarly duties, provided fidelity to reports comes first.
rows.anchor: Fakat rivayette sadakat da o vazifenin başında olmak lâzım gelir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abduh discards the mutually attested birds and stones on theoretical grounds and elevates a disconnected, isolated disease report, which Elmalılı says is not even a complete solitary report.
rows.anchor: en anûd hasımların bile inkâr edemediği irsâl-i tayr ve remy-i hacer gibi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı says errors of this scale are not ordinary human slips of independent judgment but defects in scholarly qualification that prevent trust in a person's authority as a sheikh.
rows.anchor: Böyle hatalar hasbe’l-beşeriyye her âlimde bulunması tabîî olan ictihâdî hefevât kabîlinden de değildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although Abduh's devotion to God, the Messenger, the Qur'an, and the welfare of Muslims is not in doubt, those who know the truth must warn against his major error.
rows.anchor: kelime-i ulyâ Kur’an’da olduğu, bütün rivayetler de bunu musaddık bulunduğu için ona karşı esrarşinaslık iddiasıyla ortaya atmış olduğu büyük yanlışı ihtar etmek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı offers one narrow way to read Abduh's claim of agreement: it could refer only to the final account that Ebrehe's flesh fell away until he died in San'a.
rows.anchor: bu son fıkra doğru olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A separate report says one survivor reached the Negus with news and then died there; Elmalılı considers it compatible with the final report and says the disease may have arisen later.
rows.anchor: hepsinin helâk olup ancak bir kişinin Necâşî’ye kadar giderek haberi yetiştirdikten sonra orada öldüğü hakkında da bir rivayet varsa da

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That narrow reading does not repair Abduh's earlier errors or establish his claim that the event consisted only of a smallpox or measles epidemic; it misleads readers and obscures the surah.
rows.anchor: Bu tevil evvelki sözlerindeki yanlışlığı düzeltmeyeceği gibi sözün cereyânına göre maksadına da kâfi olmaz

rows.speaker: Muhammed Abduh
rows.claim: Abduh claims the surah says smallpox or measles arose from dry stones dropped on the army by large flocks of birds sent by God with the wind.
rows.anchor: Bu sûre-i kerîme muhakkak olarak bize şunu beyan ediyor ki, o çiçek yahut kızamık

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı calls this an explicit distortion: the surah says nothing about wind, and bird flight need not depend on wind; their prompting is unknown to us.
rows.anchor: bir tahriftir, sûrede böyle bir beyan yoktur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite ṭayran denotes unfamiliar birds, while abābīl correctly suggests great companies; the text says the birds themselves aimed the stones, not merely that stones fell through them.
rows.anchor: sûrede طَيْرًا ma‘rife değil nekredir, مِنَ الطَّيْرِ değildir. Demek o zamana kadar oralarda tanınmadık garib kuşlardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling sijjīl dry or baked is partly acceptable, but the surah names neither smallpox nor any other illness; it says the army became eaten chaff after the birds struck them with stones.
rows.anchor: fakat âyette taşların kuşlar vâsıtasıyla yalnız sukūtu söylenmiyor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The resulting affliction could have been smallpox, measles, scarlet fever, plague, or an unknown disaster; armchair possibilities cannot identify it without experience or observation.
rows.anchor: hiç bilinmedik bambaşka bir âfet oluvermesi de mümkindir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent sequence is immediate death from the stones' external impact; any infection could have developed later, as Ya‘kūb b. ‘Utba reports for that year in Arabia.
rows.anchor: zâhiri taşların te’sîr-i hâricîsiyle kırılarak delik deşik dökülmüş helâk olmuş olmalarıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı concludes that Abduh's proposed account adds a claim to the revealed text rather than reporting what the surah actually says.
rows.anchor: Abduh’un bu ifadesinde de nas üzere ilâve yapmış olduğunu ma‘a’t-teessüf itiraf etmemek kābil olmaz

rows.speaker: Muhammed Abduh
rows.claim: Abduh speculates that the birds were disease-carrying flies or mosquitoes and that wind-borne, poisoned dry mud on their feet entered bodies and caused destructive sores.
rows.anchor: Abduh burada kuşları evvelâ bir sinek, sonra da bir mikrop, taşları da sinek ayağına bulaşacak kadar bir toz yapıp çıkmış

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı says Abduh successively turns birds into flies and microbes, stones into dust, and suppresses reports while changing the text to reach that conclusion.
rows.anchor: yukarıdan beri rivayetlerden onları tayy ve nassın beyânını tağyir ederek döşenişi bu neticeye gelmek olmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God owns the armies of the heavens and earth, so the event should not be explained as though flies or microbes were God's greatest forces.
rows.anchor: Bütün göklerin ve yerin cünûdu O’nundur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭayr can lexically include flying insects, but contextual clues and ordinary usage make birds the intended sense; an oath not to eat birds is not broken by swallowing a fly.
rows.anchor: sinek dilimizde de meşhur olduğu üzere uçsa da kuş değildir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Belief at issue concerns which birds the Qur'an reports in this historical event, not whether microbes exist, since microbes are matters of ordinary observation and experience.
rows.anchor: âlemde sineklerin veya mikropların varlığına itikad meselesi de değildir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No report identifies the birds as flies or microbes, and no rational necessity warrants treating the stones as dust stuck to insects' feet.
rows.anchor: bu kuşların sinek veya mikrop olduğuna dair hiçbir haber de duyulmuş değil iken

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A useful discussion could mention that eaten chaff suggests worms and corpse decay may involve microbes, while leaving the disease unidentified and stressing the extraordinary manner of destruction.
rows.anchor: ükâl, yani kurt yeme illeti ve helâk olanların lâşelerinin te‘affünâtı dolayısıyla mikroplara da işaret bulunabileceğinden bahseylemek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abduh rejects the transmitted detail while trying to present himself as explaining it, contradicting himself in pursuit of a striking interpretation no one else gave.
rows.anchor: tevâtürü tafsil edeceğim derken onu atıp خَالِفْ تـُعْرَفْ fehvâsınca kimsenin söylemediği bir söz söylemek için tenakuzlara düşmüştür

rows.speaker: Muhammed Abduh
rows.claim: Abduh argues that divine power does not depend on huge or unusual birds, special colors, or knowing the stones' number and effect, since God has every kind of force.
rows.anchor: Allah teâlâ’nın tuğyan edenleri kahretmekte kudreti eserinin zuhûru o kuşların ne dağ başları cesâmetinde olmasına

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı agrees that divine action needs no creaturely condition, but says this undermines Abduh's case: God's power depends no more on microbes or disease than on large birds.
rows.anchor: Fakat böyle olması Abduh’un davasının lehine değil, aleyhinedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although God's act needs no condition, human recognition requires some knowledge of how it appeared; believers should understand the event as the surah describes it.
rows.anchor: kudretullâhın eserinin zuhûrunu bizim bilmemiz, onun bir dereceye kadar olsun keyfiyetini bilmemize mütevakkıftır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Incomplete reports of uncertain truth should be treated as possibilities; reliable reports without a stronger contrary report may be accepted without making belief in a solitary report obligatory.
rows.anchor: Ne sıhhati ne kizbi sâbit olmayan nâkıs haberlere itikad etmeyerek ihtimal nazarıyla bakarız

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı asks why one would ignore witnesses and reports that say birds and stones, then invent flies and disease when the Qur'an's account is intelligible and possible.
rows.anchor: bütün rivayetler Kur’ân’ın dediği gibi kuşları, taşları söyleyip dururken ve kuş, taş ne demek olduğu herkesçe mâlum

rows.speaker: Muhammed Abduh
rows.claim: Abduh summarizes that God sent a means to deliver smallpox or measles to Ebrehe and his army, preserving the sanctuary and its pagan custodians until the Prophet while punishing the attackers.
rows.anchor: İşte Beyt’i yıkmak isteyen o azgın üzerine Allah teâlâ o kuşlardan ona cüderî veya hasbe maddesini îsal edecek şeyi gönderdi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı says the passage may be trusted except for the claim that God sent a disease-producing agent through the birds; that clause is wholly unsupported.
rows.anchor: o tefsir değil, usûl tâbirince ziyade ale’n-nastır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The text and neither reason nor transmitted evidence specify smallpox or measles as the stones' effect; the same sijjīl stones appear in Lot's story without such a disease-specific sense.
rows.anchor: Siccîlden taş bir madde ise de, bunun cüderî veya hasbeye bir ihtisâsı yoktur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turning the verse's direct object, birds, into disease material and changing plural references to singular carries implications that the disease substance is eternal and that God must transmit it to make disease.
rows.anchor: âyette irsâlin mef‘ûlü طَيْرًا iken onu madde-i cüderîye ve cemî‘zamirlerini müfrede tebdil eden bu ifadede

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah's evident point is that God's creative power is not bound by natural conditions; narrowing general stones to disease material to appease materialists distorts its scope.
rows.anchor: kudret-i ilâhiyenin eseri o gibi şartlara tevakkuf etmeyeceği daha demin söylenmiş iken

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı proposes saying that God sent companies of birds, had them cast extraordinary stones of formed clay, and destroyed the tyrant and army before they reached their goal.
rows.anchor: Allah teâlâ üzerlerine fırka fırka kuşlar gönderip onlara çamurdan tehaccur etmiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abduh inconsistently trusts his own unsupported interpretation while dismissing the reports that agree with the verse as unacceptable without reinterpretation; extra reports are historical detail beyond tafsir.
rows.anchor: zayıf bir rivayeti bahane ederek nazmı tağyir eder surette yapmak istediği

rows.speaker: Muhammed Abduh
rows.claim: Abduh argues that defeating a person boasting of an elephant with an unseen tiny creature would make divine power more astonishing and evident to the discerning.
rows.anchor: Bir de dört ayaklı hayvânâttan cismen en iri hayvan olan fil ile izzetlenmek isteyen bir kimsenin nazara zâhir olmayan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı notes that Abduh first made the birds flies and then microbes, but ends by describing only invisible microbes, calling this a rhetorical sophism rather than proof.
rows.anchor: Bu söz de burhânî değil, şi‘rî bir muğâlatadır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It would indeed show great power to defeat a boastful commander and a sixty-thousand-strong army with a microbe, but God created both the elephant and the microbe and displays power in ordinary and extraordinary acts.
rows.anchor: Evet, sade bir file değil, altmış bin denilen kesretli bir orduya ve mühimmâtına da güvenen bir mağruru, küçük bir mikrop ile helâk edivermek büyük bir kudret olduğunda şüphe yoktur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's power means that whatever He wills comes to be by His command Be, without needing any condition.
rows.anchor: dilediği şeyi hiçbir kayd u şarta muhtaç olmayarak bir كُنْ emriyle dilediği gibi yapıverir bir kudret olmasıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hidden cause makes God's action less apparent, while a visible cause makes it manifest; the familiar saying has Nimrod killed by a fly through brain fever.
rows.anchor: beyin humması bir sinekle mesel olmuştur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People take ordinary events for granted and could not compare an unknown microbe with an elephant; a visibly victorious small bird makes the power clearer.
rows.anchor: Böyle bir mukayesede görünen küçük bir kuşun galebesi daha bâhirdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fourteen centuries ago, when microbes were unknown, they could not serve as the event's apparent cause for its audience; the apparent cause would have been the disease itself.
rows.anchor: Bin dört yüz sene evvel, henüz insanlara mikrobun bildirilmemiş, gösterilmemiş olduğu bir zamanda

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the bird and stone verses were about invisible microbes, those details would have been useless to the original audience, and the Prophet's enemies would have attacked them.
rows.anchor: Hâlbuki file ve orduya mukabele görünmez şeylerle değil de o fili isyan ettirerek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The visible refusal of the elephant and the birds' hail-like stones made the event more manifest to ordinary people and showed divine power unconstrained by natural conditions.
rows.anchor: uzaktan yakından görülebilecek kuşlar ve dolu gibi taşlarla orduyu helâk edivermek hem âkil indinde ve hem umum indinde elbette daha zâhir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah came before witnesses to confront deniers of miracles and divine power; no one could say they had not seen the birds and stones, though later accounts mention smallpox, measles, or poisonous trees.
rows.anchor: hârikaları inkâr eden ve Hâlık’ın kudretini şirk ile takyîde kalkışan azgınlara

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı asks whether fluent Arabs could have understood birds and stones as invisible microbes, and says translators who render the verse as microbe-bearing stones were misled.
rows.anchor: diye terceme eden bazı mütercimlerin aldanışına acınmaz mı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He condemns hostile caricatures that call the stones bird droppings and claim panic alone destroyed the army, as well as efforts to discredit the Prophet with fabricated travel stories.
rows.anchor: taşları tırtıl gibi kuş tersleri diye istihzâ ederek onunla bir ordunun korkudan panik oluverdiğini söz diye söylemekten utanmayan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although later readers may dismiss the event as a tale, denying it was difficult before hostile contemporaries who watched for any chance to refute the Prophet; even his enemies then neither denied nor reinterpreted it.
rows.anchor: O zaman Peygamber’e her taraftan gayz püsküren düşmanları bile ne inkâra ne tevile sapmamışken

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı quotes a couplet admonishing friendly doubters to defend the truth at least as strongly as an enemy would.
rows.anchor: Düşman kadar olsun siper et sûret-i hakkı Ey dost, Hüseyin olmaz isen bari Yezid ol

rows.speaker: İbn İshak
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq, as recorded by Ibn Hisham, says that after God repelled the Abyssinians, Arabs exalted Quraysh as God's people and poets described God's defeat of the attackers' plan.
rows.anchor: İbn Hişâm’ın kayd u zabt ettiği üzere İbn İshak demiştir ki

rows.speaker: Abdullah b. Ziba‘ra
rows.claim: Ziba‘ra's poem treats Mecca's sanctuary as inviolable, asks the Abyssinian ruler what he saw, and says sixty thousand did not return alive, including the sick.
rows.anchor: Ezcümle Abdullah b. Ziba‘ra b. Adî b. Kays b. Adî şöyle demişti

rows.speaker: Ebu Kays Sayfî b. Eslet
rows.claim: Elmalılı cites Sayfî's poem among the contemporary verses recounting the Abyssinian elephant episode and God's hail sent upon them.
rows.anchor: Ebu Kays Sayfî b. Eslet b. Cüşem b. Vâil de şöyle demiştir

rows.speaker: Ümeyye b. Ebu’s-Salt
rows.claim: Elmalılı cites Umayya's poem affirming God's signs and describing the elephant held at Mughammis, crawling as if wounded, before the army scattered.
rows.anchor: Haniflerden Ümeyye b. Ebu’s-Salt b. Ebû Rebî‘a Sekafî de şöyle demiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The central lesson is that an aggressive army, about to reach Mecca with no visible human defense, had all its plans frustrated by God just as it approached its goal.
rows.anchor: önüne geleni çiğneyen saldırıcı bir ordunun tam Mekke’nin yanına gelip de hedef ve maksadına vâsıl olmak üzere bulunduğu gün

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The birds and stones are supporting details that make the divine nature of the action explicit; even the polytheists attributed the extraordinary outcome to God.
rows.anchor: Diğer âyetler, kuşların akını, taşların yağdırılışı da bunun mahza taraf-ı rabbânîden olduğunu en açık bir surette izhar için

rows.speaker: Fahr-ı Râzî
rows.claim: Razi asks why God punished the army that intended to damage the Kaaba when Quraysh had long filled it with idols, a worse offense against the sanctuary.
rows.anchor: Küffâr-ı Kureyş eski bir zamandan beri Kâbe’yi putlarla doldurmuş değil miydiler?

rows.speaker: Fahr-ı Râzî
rows.claim: Razi answers that idolatry violates God's rights, whereas destroying the Kaaba violates people's rights; the worldly penalty targets highway robbers, rebels, and murderers, but not harmless old, blind, monastic, or female unbelievers.
rows.anchor: Kâbe’ye putları koymak Hakkullâh’a te‘addî

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı summarizes that worldly punishment in divine law follows harm to people's rights, while punishment for matters solely God's right is principally in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: şer‘-i ilâhîde dünyevî cezâ, hukūk-ı ibâda zarar ve tecavüz dolayısıyladır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The event prepared for the birth and mission of the Messenger who would spread God's religion; after this surah addressing the Prophet, the Quraysh surah follows.
rows.anchor: Allah dininin neşri için dünyaya gelmek üzere bulunan Resûlullah’ın vilâdetine bir mukaddime

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı's rendering keeps īlāf in the phrase about Quraysh's journeys, then reads the verses as calling them to worship the Lord of the House who fed them from hunger and secured them from fear.
rows.anchor: Meâl: Îlâfı için Kureyş’in (1) sefere îlâfları yazın kışın (2). Hiç olmazsa onun için kulluk etsinler Rabbine bu Beyt’in

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The canonical rasm of the Uthmanic codices writes īlāf without some medial alifs; early Kufic scribes regularly omitted such alifs, while Basran and later practice usually wrote them.
rows.anchor: Kûfî hattatların kudemâsı, mütevassıt eliflerin hepsini muttariden hazfederler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though later copies may show alifs for ease, Qur'anic orthography has distinctive forms that must be preserved; Elmalılı gives the original spelling used here.
rows.anchor: Kur’an imlâsının birçok yerlerde Arabî hat kāidelerine dahi uymayan hususiyetleri bulunduğu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ithaf says all codices retain the yā in the first īlāf, omit it in the second, and omit the alif before fā in both forms.
rows.anchor: Yani Hazret-i Osman mushaflarının hepsi bunun üzerinde müttefiktir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spelling likely preserves three canonical readings without changing the written form: Abu Ja‘far softens the first hamza to a kasra yā and reads the second with hamza but no yā.
rows.anchor: ikincisi يا’sız hemze ile إِۦلَٰفِهِمْ okunur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ‘Amir reads the first form with hamza but no yā and the second with hamza and yā; the remaining readings pronounce both with hamza and yā.
rows.anchor: İbn Âmir kıraatinde de birincisi يا’sız hemze ile لإلَاف ikincisi hemze ve يا ile sâir kıraatler gibi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All readings derive from ilf and ulfat: īlāf can be an active or passive Form IV verbal noun meaning habituating or being habituated, or a Form III noun meaning reciprocal familiarity, agreement, or pact.
rows.anchor: if‘âl babından ülfet ettirmek mânasına masdar-ı ma‘lûm

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the majority reading appears Form IV, many commentators understand īlāf as habituating or being habituated, with Quraysh genitive potentially marking either object or subject.
rows.anchor: Ekser kıraate göre zâhiri if‘âl babından göründüğü için çokları ülfet ettirmek veya ettirilmek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some commentators insist on the reciprocal pact sense for both words, using Abu Ja‘far's and Ibn ‘Amir's readings as evidence that the readings explain one another.
rows.anchor: Ebû Cafer ve İbn Âmir kıraatleri karînesiyle ikisinin de mufâ‘ale bâbından mu‘âhede mânasına

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qamus defines īlāf as a pact or safe-conduct arrangement like a pledge of security for caravans, including protection and permission for safe passage; this favors taking Quraysh as the subject.
rows.anchor: Bunda Kureyş’e izâfeti fâiline izâfet olmak zâhirdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı keeps īlāf untranslated because it has both a customary technical sense and a broader meaning, and should not be restricted to habituation or to pact-making alone.
rows.anchor: mealde aynen muhafazasını daha muvâfık ve doğru bulduk

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Raghib explains ulfat as gathering together through joining and harmony; habituation, continuity, affinity, and making a pact are implications or related uses of that basic sense.
rows.anchor: i’tilâf mânasına isim olup aslında iltiyâm ile ictimâ‘dır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Accordingly, Quraysh's īlāf can mean their being accustomed or made accustomed, or their making and being made to make agreements with one another or other peoples.
rows.anchor: Binâen‘aleyh ايلاَف قـُرَيْشٍ Kureyş’i alıştırmak, ısındırmak, Kureyş’in alıştırılması, alışması demek olabileceği gibi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh is the famous tribe descended from Nadr within Kinana, Mudar, and Adnan; Alusi quotes Qurtubi calling this the soundest and most established view, also held by some jurists.
rows.anchor: “akvâlin esah ve esbeti” demiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu al-Fida and others give the sounder, majority view that Quraysh are descendants of Fihr b. Malik b. Nadr, excluding those not descended from Fihr; Zubayr b. Bakkar says genealogists agree.
rows.anchor: sahih olan; Kureyş Fihr b. Mâlik b. Nadr b. Kinâne evlâdıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With qāf fatḥa, qarsh can mean cutting, collecting scattered things and joining them, or intermingling spears in battle; taqārush is spears crossing and tekarrush means gathering.
rows.anchor: kesmek ve şuradan buradan birtakım şeyler toplayıp birbirine zamm u ilhak ederek karıştırmak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With qāf kasra, qirsh is said to name a sea monster that devours other sea creatures; its diminutive is quraysh, a name or epithet given to Fihr for strength.
rows.anchor: deniz canavarlarından birinin ismi imiş ki deryâdaki diğer hayvanları yer

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says the name arose after Qusay regrouped the dispersed tribe, recovered the Kaaba keys from Khuza'a, and restored its status; on Ibn Sa‘id's account Quraysh names Fihr's descendants, not Fihr himself.
rows.anchor: bu dağılmış olan kabileyi derleyip toplayarak Huzâ‘îlerden Kâbe’nin anahtarlarını istirdad ederek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ferrā and Ibn Hisham derive Quraysh from tekarrush as trade and earning; a Rajaz by Ru‘ba uses qurūsh for commerce and gain, which Elmalılı notes resembles Turkish kuruş.
rows.anchor: ticaretlerinden dolayı tekessüb mânasına

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi also attributes the name to takrīsh, inspecting and meeting needs, because Quraysh traditionally looked after petitioners' needs and pilgrims' deficiencies.
rows.anchor: çünkü bunların atalarından beri ihtiyaç sâhiplerinin hâcetlerini teftiş ederek arayıp sormak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı says the diminutive Quraysh is honorific, like the well-known honorific diminutive duwayhiya; Hashim and his brother greatly served Quraysh's īlāf.
rows.anchor: tasğîrin tâzim için olduğunda söz yoktur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's genealogy runs through Hashim, Qusay, Fihr, Kinana, Mudar, and Adnan to Ishmael and Abraham, making him Ibrahimite, Ismailite, Adnani, Mudari, Kinani, Qurayshi, and Hashimi.
rows.anchor: neseb-i nebevî dahi İbrâhîmî, İsmâîlî, Adnânî, Mudarî, Kinânî, Kureşî, Hâşimîdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Given Qusay's and Hashim's service in bringing Quraysh together and God's care for the House and its people in the elephant event, Quraysh should have led in accepting the Prophet's call to monotheism; their initial resistance occasioned this surah.
rows.anchor: yine ilk evvel onların şirkte ısrar ederek muhalefet ve mümâna‘ata kıyam etmeleri bu sûrenin sebeb-i nüzûlü olmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation makes the lām a marker of wonder attached to an omitted command: marvel that Quraysh are accustomed to seasonal journeys yet do not worship the Lord of this House.
rows.anchor: taaccüb için olup mahzuf اعجبوا fiiline müte‘allik olmaktır ki

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This wonder reading suits the surah's independence and the consequence expressed by let them worship, though it is less apt because it can suggest that the journeys themselves are blameworthy.
rows.anchor: Bu mâna sûrenin istiklâline ve فَلْيَعْبُدُوا۟ emrinin tefrî‘ine nazaran münâsib bir mâna olmakla beraber

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second interpretation takes the lām as causal and, as the passage ends, Elmalılı notes that this reading has two sub-interpretations.
rows.anchor: 2. Ta‘lîl için olmaktır, bunda da iki vecih vardır
